key_insight: A multimodal self-supervised EEG foundation model can learn seizure-relevant representations that transfer well across datasets and tasks.
clinical_relevance: This could improve seizure detection systems by making them more adaptable to new patients and recording settings, while also supporting more interpretable localization.
method: Raw EEG encoded with a Mamba-based model
Time-frequency EEG encoded with a ViT-style branch
Text encoder + shared embedding space with masked modeling, cross-view contrastive alignment, and temporal consistency losses
evidence_signal: The best model reached AUROC 0.874 on the CHB-MIT benchmark, the ensemble reached 0.878, and leave-one-subject-out testing showed mean balanced accuracy of 0.558 across 19 subjects.
watch_item: Performance dropped substantially in patient-independent LOSO evaluation, so real-world generalization may still be limited despite strong benchmark results.
paper_title: Multimodal Pretraining for Generalizable EEG Representation Learning
